text: Smooth particle mesh Ewald / SPME SPME approximates Ewald structure factors using smooth cardinal B-splines. Treat it as a specific interpolation-and-force construction rather than a synonym for every PME implementation. Problem and representative equations Let uᵢ be particle coordinates in mesh units and Mₚ a cardinal B-spline of order p, not degree p. The product below is the local tensor assignment in three dimensions. Fourier structure factors require a correction for the spline response. Qmxmymz=∑iqi∏d∈{x,y,z}Mp(uid−md),deg⁡Mp=p−1.Qmx​my​mz​​=i∑​qi​d∈{x,y,z}∏​Mp​(uid​−md​),degMp​=p−1. Algorithm Spread charge over p neighboring mesh points in each direction, evaluate a corrected reciprocal mesh energy by FFT, and obtain forces using derivatives of the assignment in analytical differentiation. Record the spline order and mesh together with whether differentiation is analytical or in Fourier space. Conditions and pitfalls Smooth assignment alone does not guarantee both energy consistency and exact net-force cancellation. Ewald neutrality, boundary and self-term conventions still apply. Comparisons with original PME should control error tolerance and differentiation rules, not merely the number of mesh points. The companion also uses analytical energy gradients with B-spline orders 4/6. Discrete energy–force consistency, common-translation mesh effects and net force are separate observables. Finite-mesh aliasing generally permits nonzero net force; exact momentum conservation is not claimed. What to check Measure force errors against the same converged Ewald reference and check energy finite differences. Report common-translation mesh effects and total force separately. Ensure real-space truncation is not hiding the reciprocal-space convergence trend. The design compares 16³/24³/40³ meshes and several common translations against matching direct-Ewald and independent theta references. It separates partition of unity/charge, energy differences, RMS/maximum force errors and real-space truncation; it supplies no evidence for long MD or original PME. Check fixed inputs: separate scoped releases Check each example’s inputs, observables, diagnostic definitions and scope. What a passing check establishes depends on its acceptance criteria and differs from a general mathematical guarantee. Historical inputs, measurements and criteria are preserved. Mesh/order convergence of B-spline smooth PME Computation for a fixed target A small smooth-PME example assigns charge with B-splines and evaluates the Ewald reciprocal contribution by FFT. Finite-mesh aliasing permits nonzero net force for this energy-gradient variant; that diagnostic is reported. No exact momentum conservation, long MD, original PME, optimized P³M or slab validation is claimed.
